description:
Redwood Inference is standardizing how it represents model and version metadata across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments, and using that metadata to automatically generate customer-visible release notes (a “model changelog”). Today, model updates are communicated inconsistently (docs pages, ad-hoc Slack messages, occasional runtime release notes), which creates customer confusion during rollouts/A/B tests, complicates support escalations, and makes enterprise change-management harder.

Goals:
- Define a canonical Model Metadata Schema (v1) that covers identity, provenance, compatibility, performance, safety/policy notes, and deprecation fields for every model version served by Redwood.
- Establish a single source of truth for changes (additions/updates/deprecations) and an automated changelog generator that produces customer-facing release notes and machine-readable feeds.
- Integrate changelog outputs into Redwood Console (model catalog + rollouts pages), docs site, and APIs/SDKs (e.g., headers/fields for pinned version + changelog URL).
- Ensure enterprise requirements: auditability (who changed what, when), immutability/retention, RBAC for internal editors, and a review workflow (product + release engineering + support readiness).

Scope:
- In scope: schema definition, migration of existing model registry records, changelog generator pipeline, templating rules for customer-safe text, review/approval workflow, console/docs integrations, and observability for the pipeline.
- Out of scope (initially): fully automated natural-language “what changed in quality” narratives from eval diffs (only links/metrics in v1), per-customer customized release notes, and real-time streaming of changelog events (batch/daily is acceptable for v1).

Stakeholders and teams:
- Product (Console & Rollouts): defines customer-facing requirements and approval gates (Marissa Cole, Paula Mendes).
- Engineering (Console/Control Plane/Model Catalog): implements schema, APIs, console views (Dylan Brooks, Chloe Martin, Jada Williams, Quentin Harris, Ethan Park).
- Release Engineering: aligns with release trains and change-management (Connor O’Brien).
- Developer Experience/Docs: docs-site integration, style guide, public-facing wording conventions (Elliot Price, Wei Chen, Kira Thompson).
- Support/Customer Success: support readiness, known-issues docs, escalation patterns.
- Security & Compliance: audit events, retention, access controls for enterprise expectations.

Timeline (hypothetical):
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): requirements gathering + draft schema and ADRs.
- Phase 1 (4–6 weeks): implement schema in model registry + migration tooling + internal review workflow.
- Phase 2 (4 weeks): changelog generator pipeline + docs-site output + console integration behind a feature flag.
- Phase 3 (2–3 weeks): API/SDK surfaces + enterprise audit/retention hardening + launch readiness.

Key deliverables:
- Confluence: schema standard, ADRs, change-management policy, runbook.
- GitHub: schema + migrations, generator service, console/docs/SDK integrations.
- Linear: execution plan and rollout milestones.
- Slack/Gmail/Fireflies/HubSpot/Jira: realistic coordination, customer requests, and support loops that motivate and validate the work.

files.description: Primary design spec: proposed Model Metadata Schema v1 fields (identity, versioning, provenance, quantization, context window, tool/function calling compatibility, deprecations), examples, migration strategy, and open questions.
Formal internal standard describing required/optional metadata fields, validation rules, naming conventions (model_id/version_id), and compatibility guarantees across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
ADR deciding the changelog source of truth (model registry + signed change events) vs. git tags/docs-only, with rationale, trade-offs, and implications for auditing and enterprise needs.
Service doc for the model registry metadata service: APIs, storage, schema validation, auth/RBAC, event emission for changes, and operational ownership.
How-to guide for operators/release engineers: triggering the generator, reviewing drafts, approving publication, and rollback steps if a note is incorrect.
Guidance on aligning runtime release notes with model version notes (e.g., when a runtime upgrade changes kernels/throughput for specific models) and cross-linking practices.
Customer-safe release notes style guide: templates, do/don’t language, prohibited internal details, and required sections (impact, compatibility, deprecation timelines, links to dashboards/evals).
Audit logging spec: event types for model metadata create/update/deprecate, required fields for SIEM export, retention/immutability expectations, and access controls.
Support-facing doc capturing early limitations (e.g., missing historical notes pre-migration), common customer questions, and recommended messaging/workarounds.
Internal policy for announcing model changes: review gates, timelines for deprecations, required changelog entries, and escalation path for urgent hotfixes.
Product requirements doc: user stories for customers (pinning, transparency, rollbacks), non-goals, MVP criteria, and measurable success metrics (support ticket reduction, adoption).
Operational runbook: alerts, failure modes (bad schema validation, publish failures, docs sync lag), dashboards, and step-by-step remediation.
Working doc with early brainstorming: field lists, edge cases from rollouts/A-B testing, notes from stakeholder interviews, and unresolved questions.
Implementation plan draft: pipeline stages (diff detection, templating, approval, publish), data flow diagrams, and rough milestones tied to Linear issues.
Sheet-like artifact represented as a table: experiments comparing generation approaches, failure rates, publish latency, and required manual edits.
PRD draft: UX requirements for Console (model page changelog tab, filters by date/version, export), approval workflow requirements, and launch stages.
Launch checklist: comms plan, documentation updates, support enablement, feature flag rollout, and post-launch metrics to monitor.
Spreadsheet-style list of customer requests: which accounts asked for model change transparency, what formats they want (RSS, API, console), and urgency.
Security/compliance notes: how changelog entries are stored, tamper-evidence approach, retention durations, and how to answer typical enterprise questionnaires.
Draft of proposed metrics/alerts: publish lag, validation failures, percent of changes with human edits, broken links, and customer-facing error monitoring.
Engineering epic: “Model metadata schema + changelog generator” with scope breakdown, owners, acceptance criteria, and links to Confluence spec.
Implement schema validation in model registry (required fields, versioned schema, backward compatibility strategy).
Add change-event emission for metadata updates (diff format, event IDs, audit fields) to feed the generator.
Migration tooling: backfill metadata for existing catalog entries, including provenance and compatibility matrices.
Changelog generator service: template rules, customer-safe redaction, and publish targets (docs site + console API).
Console integration: add “Changelog” tab to model/version pages and link to rollout history; gated behind a feature flag.
API contract: expose model_version + changelog_url in responses/headers for OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
Observability: dashboards and alerting for generator pipeline health and publish lag.
Security/RBAC: restrict who can edit model metadata fields and who can approve/publish customer-visible notes.
PM issue: define customer-facing release note taxonomy (bugfix vs perf vs compatibility vs deprecation) and required sections per change type.
PM issue: approval workflow requirements (who signs off, SLAs for review, emergency publish path) and success metrics.
PM issue: enterprise requirements gathering for auditability/immutability and how it maps to Console and docs.
Design task: Console UI mocks for model changelog browsing (filters, version compare, export/share link).
Design task: docs-site information architecture for model release notes (per model, per date, RSS/feed entry points).
PR: Introduce schema_v1 structs and validation rules for model/version records; adds unit tests and migration scaffolding.
PR: Add metadata diffing + change-event emission (with actor, timestamp, and event_id) for create/update/deprecate operations.
PR: Backfill script to populate missing provenance/compatibility fields for top 50 catalog models; includes dry-run mode and audit summary output.
PR: Add deprecation fields (sunset_date, replacement_model, customer_messaging) and enforce constraints in validation.
PR: Add immutable “public_changelog_fields” allowlist and redaction logic to prevent accidental leakage of internal-only metadata.
PR: Control plane API to fetch model changelog entries by model_id/version_id with pagination and filtering.
PR: Add approval workflow endpoints (draft -> in_review -> published) and role checks for release-note publication.
PR: Implement changelog generator worker: consumes model change-events, renders templates, stores drafts, and links to docs publish job.
PR: Add audit log entries for model metadata changes and publish actions; includes SIEM export field mapping.
PR: Console backend: add changelog endpoints used by UI; supports feature flag and account-tier gating.
PR: Add rollout UI integration hooks so rollouts reference a model version’s published changelog entry at time of change.
PR: Add rate-limited public feed endpoint (JSON) for changelog entries; includes caching and ETags.
PR: Fix generator edge case: multiple metadata updates in one day collapsing incorrectly; introduces deterministic ordering by event_id.
PR: Add integration tests for schema validation + generator publish flow in staging; includes CI job and fixtures.
PR: Add “customer_safe_summary” templating improvements (limit jargon, ensure compatibility notes always present).
PR: Implement rollback for published changelog entries (supersede with corrected entry, preserve history) to satisfy audit requirements.
PR: Add metrics + tracing for generator pipeline (publish lag, validation failures, docs sync failures) and wire to dashboards.
PR: Surface model version + changelog URL via response headers/fields for OpenAI-compatible routes; includes compatibility notes.
PR: SDK: expose resolved model_version and changelog_url in response objects; update docs and examples.
PR: TS SDK: add changelog link passthrough and typed structures for model metadata; includes minor breaking-change note.
PR: Add model release notes section to docs site; new navigation and per-model landing pages generated from published feed.
PR: Add style linting for release notes templates and forbid internal-only fields; includes CI rule.
PR: Add RSS/Atom feed generation for model changelog and documentation on how customers subscribe.
PR: Update Dedicated/Private docs to reference changelog and change-management expectations; includes screenshots of Console UI.
PR: Add dashboard panels for changelog generator health (publish lag, error rate, approvals backlog) and recommended alerts.
